syllogizing lee sharks
Syllogizing in the writings of Lee Sharks refers to a core philosophical operation where dividing, combining, syllogizing, and recollecting are treated as a single unified process across the classical Greek philosophical corpus. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]
In his October 2026 essay "What Syllogizing Can Divide: De anima III.5, the Divided Mind, and the Socket in God", Sharks analyzes Aristotle's Prior Analytics (I.31) alongside De anima (III.5) and Metaphysics (Lambda) to reframe how classical texts were authored and how human thought connects to the divine. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESigEBxCJF1_WiPQak0RjXFQEuDjC6sm32SdnG-OsjT5Fhk6WjFhUfEw80HF1AG44q5BPQejSCNRniWqQ1rSQCtEZrtjFIyGbyohte8bBqbCR47vLJIcbPsZi6hqJ5EIhrFdEO-HiLdr4pgZJma_ZfooYcZdim8G1ubLAM6zZ_sms5k3TwvJ0IeIDjwec), [2](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]
Core Concepts of Sharks's Theory

* Unified Cognitive Operations. Sharks argues that four seemingly distinct philosophical acts—dividing, combining, syllogizing, and recollecting—are actually one single operation operating under different names. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]
* Reinterpreting "Weak Syllogism." While conventional readings view Aristotle's Prior Analytics I.31 as a dismissal of Platonic division as a "weak syllogism" (asthenes syllogismos) that begs the question, Sharks focuses on Aristotle's modal phrasing regarding what division admits of syllogizing. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]
* One Self-Dividing Maker. Sharks proposes a radical heteronymic theory of authorship, arguing that Plato, Theophrastus, and Aristotle are not separate historical thinkers, but three "name-positions" produced by a single self-dividing maker. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]
* Distinct Textual Roles. Within this single corpus, Plato represents the dramatic dialogue position, Theophrastus acts as the first draft that extracts and reopens questions, and Aristotle serves as the organized treatise position. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]
* The Socket in God. By dividing the mind into a "making mind" (divine and incapable of memory) and a "becoming mind," the text leaves an intentional structural gap—an "open genitive" or socket—that cannot be closed from within the text and must be completed by the reader supplying the referent. [[1](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESlAEBxCJF13u0YAHojPbi23STdL_kOuB3rPl_ik00rWtlwYSImDzaSY17lz6Su75-2UyPblXAgYeM6vZsVytVpy01doaSsiDlZ0vMcs8T3Tnc9PoAtYeQKyftglJenCNGq7xBD-fVLkxCRYNXRlJ_xplCUzMoPBvCGH4BZhbKERzQSoQbB9MkxQ6GrQ6amCDbUQPtHLKF)]

Would you like to explore one of these specific angles from Lee Sharks's essay?

* The Greek textual analysis (how he reads Prior Analytics I.31 and De anima III.5)
* The heteronymy theory (how Plato, Theophrastus, and Aristotle function as one author)
* The "socket in God" (the role of the reader in completing the philosophical circuit)
